**[P1] Do not let the newest receipt refresh every unit’s source binding**

This only proves that the workspace has not changed since the last review, not that each unit’s current source was reviewed.

Reproduction: review `alpha`, review `beta`, edit `beta`, then review `alpha` again. The new global fingerprint matches the workspace, while the old `beta` receipt remains in `reviewedUnits`, so approval succeeds with unreviewed `beta` changes. A receipt for an unknown unit can produce the same result.

Please use unit-scoped source bindings or require an explicit final workspace-wide review rather than allowing one receipt to validate all older per-unit receipts.

Reproduced your exact scenario (and its inverse — re-reviewing an earlier unit after tampering a later one) and fixed at fe0810cb: every consecutive fingerprint transition in a multi-receipt chain must now be a pure addition, not just the newest-matches-current check. See the summary comment above for the full explanation; both orderings are now covered by regression tests.

Update, and it is a retraction of what I wrote here earlier: I'm removing `fingerprintChainIsAdditionsOnly`. Your finding stands — the newest-matches-current comparison alone does not prove each unit's current source was reviewed, and with the rule gone your exact sequence (review `alpha`, review `beta`, edit `beta`, re-review `alpha`) passes again. I'm not claiming otherwise, and I'd rather say that plainly than leave this thread reading as fixed.

The reason is that the rule I built for it is wrong in both directions, and I reproduced both at `6300ad3b` before deciding.

It refuses work the protocol itself mandates. `stage-protocol.md` §12a requires recording a NOT-READY receipt, re-invoking the lead to fix the artifact **in place**, then re-reviewing. Fixing in place is an `M` transition, so the chain fails closed even though the reviewer inspected exactly the current tree:

```
newest == current: true
transition       : "M\talpha.ts"
approve          : rc 1  source-fingerprint mismatch
```

And it still does not prove review. A file written after `alpha`'s review and read by nobody is a pure addition, so the chain check passes and approve returns rc 0. So the rule buys a false refusal of the normal rework loop and of any second unit that touches a shared file, without closing the hole it was built for. Two further failures are in the summary comment above: re-review can never clear the chain once a transition is in it, and the recorded-repo layout — which is the default, since sibling auto-discovery populates `repos` at intent birth — produces a composite hash that is not a diffable git object at all.

Where that leaves your finding:

- It is documented, not buried. The CHANGELOG bullet and `docs/reference/12-state-machine.md` claimed the stronger property; both now state that a match proves only that the current tree is identical to the one the newest recorded review inspected, not that each unit was reviewed against its own code. The same paragraph goes in `verifyReviewerPrecondition`'s comment block.
- Your repro survives as a permanent test, inverted rather than deleted — same scenario, asserting the documented behaviour, citing this round. When attribution lands it goes red on purpose.
- It is genuinely fixed on one route already: `aidlc-swarm.ts` finalize compares each claimed unit's terminal receipt against **its own Bolt worktree's** fingerprint, which is the unit-scoped binding you asked for. It is the stage-level route where the hash is workspace-global and the receipts are per unit.
- Your other finding here — the `:(glob)**/aidlc/**` pathspec swallowing real source — stays closed, and this round tightened it further: the exclusion was still being applied inside every recorded sibling repo and inside submodules, where a directory of that name is application source. Fixed, with repros.
- Follow-up for the real fix is #662. It needs a machine-readable manifest of the source paths each unit wrote; `code-summary` has that in prose only and there is no such manifest in `core/tools/` or `core/hooks/` today, which is why I don't think it fits in this PR.

This leans on #629's criterion being conditional — "ambiguous attribution fails closed **or follows an explicitly documented policy**" — and I've taken the documented-policy branch. That is a judgement call on a finding you raised, so if you'd rather I keep a fail-closed rule and fix the flows it breaks instead, or hold the PR until attribution exists, say so and I'll do that.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
[P1] Reject control characters in audit field names

Only the exact key `Event` is rejected, while field names are rendered verbatim. I reproduced an allowed `ERROR_LOGGED` append using a field name containing `\n**Event`, which `findAllEvents()` then recognized as a forged `HUMAN_TURN`. The same path can forge `UNIT_COMPLETED` or any protected receipt. Validate field names against a strict single-line grammar before rendering.

[P1] Validate units against the authoritative DAG

`unit start` accepts any nonempty unit name without checking the resolved Bolt DAG. I started `rogue-unit`; `next` then routed legitimate `unit-a`, but starting it failed because the rogue checkpoint remained active. This leaves the workflow deadlocked. Require a safe unit identifier that exists in the authoritative unit set, and reject newlines/path traversal in all state-mirrored values.

[P2] Require human presence before recording rejection

The rejection path now rejects cancellation boilerplate, but it still never calls `humanActedSinceGate()`. A conductor can submit any substantive generated feedback and commit `GATE_REJECTED` without a human turn, even though this receipt is treated as authority-bearing and consumes presence for later decisions. Apply the same human-presence guard used by approval.

**MAJOR (latent)** (same at lines 116 and 128): the anchor payload is interpolated into `new RegExp` verbatim - no escaping, and the parser accepts any `\S+`. Two failure modes:

- `after-step:1.5` builds `/^### Step 1.5\b.*$/m`, where `.` matches any character, so it can splice at the wrong step.
- `after-step:)` throws a SyntaxError from `new RegExp`; there is no try/catch around `locateAnchor`, so the throw unwinds all three loops and aborts every remaining fragment - and `compose.sh` runs the script with `2>/dev/null || true`, so the partial compose is silent.

Suggested fix: add a tiny `escapeRegExp` and use it at all three sites; optionally validate anchors at parse time (`after-step`/`before-step` payload must be `^\w+$`) and skip-with-error rather than throw.

Fixed in `fb50f0d`. Anchors are now validated against a closed pattern and `escapeRegExp`-quoted before going into `new RegExp` (`locateAnchor` in `compose.ts`). `after-step:1.5` no longer treats `.` as a wildcard, and a malformed/unknown anchor is skipped-and-logged to the drops file rather than throwing a `SyntaxError`.

**[MAJOR, blocking] `plugin build` recursively deletes whatever outDir it is pointed at.**

The rmSync pre-clean was fine while the only callers were internal (dist/plugins and mkdtemp paths), but the new subcommand exposes it to arbitrary CLI input: `bun scripts/package.ts plugin build test-pro claude .` wipes the current directory before writing the projection (reproduced against a scratch dir; exit 0, prior contents gone). A guard is one conditional: refuse a non-empty outDir that does not contain a prior projection marker (the manifestDir is a natural one), or require an explicit `--force`.

Fixed in `54faa29`. The subcommand now guards outDir: it refuses a non-empty dir that is not itself a prior projection (no `<manifestDir>/`) unless `--force`, so `plugin build test-pro claude .` now errors with cwd contents intact (reproduced — important.txt survives). Also added proper usage errors for an unknown plugin (`unknown plugin "…" (have: test-pro)`) and unknown harness, replacing the raw ENOENT/rmSync stack. t188 still green (it builds into a fresh temp subdir).
